items.q: Q1. Can Indian students pursue pharmacy studies in Sweden?
items.a: Yes. Indian students can apply if they meet academic, subject specific and language requirements. Most professional pharmacy programs require knowledge of Swedish. **Pharmacy in Sweden for Indian Students** requires careful planning of academic qualifications and language preparation.

items.q: Q2. Are there pharmacies in English in Sweden?
items.a: Some pharmaceutical science and related research programs may be taught in English language. Uppsala University offers the main professional programs in pharmacy in Swedish. A degree in pharmaceutical science taught in English does not necessarily lead to a licence to practise as a pharmacist.

items.q: Q3. What is the duration of the pharmacy degree in Sweden?
items.a: Uppsala University offers a three-year Pharmacy program leading to a Bachelor’s degree. The program amounts to 180 ECTS credits. Its professional Master of Science Program in Pharmacy is a 300 credit, five-year program.

items.q: Q4. How much does it cost to study pharmacy in Sweden?
items.a: For non-EU/EEA students required to pay tuition fees, the three-year bachelor’s pharmacy program at Uppsala University has a total tuition fee of SEK 450,000. The five-year professional program has a separate fee structure and students should confirm the latest official fees. Students should check the latest **Pharmacy Fees in Sweden** before making their study plans.

items.q: Q5. After BPharm or MPharm, can Indian pharmacy graduates work in Sweden?
items.a: Possibly. Indian pharmacy graduates must fulfill the relevant qualification assessment and Swedish licensing requirements including language skills and any required tests or further training. A degree in pharmacy does not automatically confer a right to practice professionally in Sweden.
